questions.subtopic: Necessity of Political Parties Thought Experiment
questions.question: Imagine a situation without political parties where every candidate in an election is independent. What would be the major consequence?
options: All public corruption would vanish instantly overnight
No one will be able to make any promises to the people about any major policy changes, and no one will be responsible for how the country will be run
Economic growth would accelerate to 100% per annum
Elections would be completely free of any financial expenditure
questions.explanation: If every candidate is independent, no one will be able to make any promises to the people about any major policy changes. The government may be formed, but its utility will remain ever uncertain. Elected representatives will be accountable to their constituency for what they do in the locality, but no one will be responsible for how the country will be run.

questions.question: Why has India evolved a Multi-Party System rather than a one-party or two-party system?
options: Because the Constitution bans any two parties from merging
Because Indian voters are required to register in at least three parties simultaneously
Because multi-party systems eliminate the need for an Election Commission
Because the vast social and geographical diversity in such a large country cannot be easily absorbed by two or three parties
questions.explanation: Party system is not something any country can choose. India has evolved a multi-party system because the social and geographical diversity in such a large country is not easily absorbed by two or even three parties.

questions.subtopic: First Challenge: Lack of Internal Democracy
questions.question: The first major challenge faced by political parties in India is the 'lack of internal democracy'. This primarily manifests as:
options: Concentration of power in one or a few top leaders; parties do not hold regular organizational elections or maintain membership registers
Voters being barred from voting on voting day
The Supreme Court drafting political manifestos
All party members receiving identical government salaries
questions.explanation: All over the world there is a tendency in political parties towards the concentration of power in one or few leaders at the top. Parties do not keep membership registers, do not hold organisational meetings, and do not conduct internal elections regularly.

questions.question: The challenge of 'Dynastic Succession' in political parties refers to the practice where:
options: Ministers are chosen exclusively from the civil service
Top positions are always controlled by members of one family, denying ordinary workers fair opportunity to rise
Political leaders pass an annual physical fitness test
Party presidency changes every month by lottery
questions.explanation: Since most political parties do not practice open and transparent procedures for their functioning, there are very few ways for an ordinary worker to rise to the top. Those who happen to be the leaders are in a position of unfair advantage to favour people close to them or even their family members.

questions.subtopic: Third Challenge: Money and Muscle Power
questions.question: The growing role of 'money and muscle power' in political parties during elections results in:
options: The abolition of all private banks in India
The elimination of electronic voting machines
A complete ban on television election news broadcasts
Parties nominating rich candidates or criminals who can raise funds and win seats, rather than ideologically committed workers
questions.explanation: Since parties are focused only on winning elections, they tend to use short-cuts to win elections. They tend to nominate those candidates who have or can raise lots of money. Rich people and companies who give funds to the parties tend to have influence on the policies and decisions of the party. In some cases, parties support criminals who can win elections.

questions.subtopic: Fourth Challenge: Lack of Meaningful Choice
questions.question: The fourth challenge to political parties is that very often they do not seem to offer a 'meaningful choice' to voters. Why is this so in recent decades?
options: All parties use identical election symbols on the ballot
Candidates are chosen by foreign ambassadors
There is a significant ideological convergence where major parties agree on fundamental economic policies, differing only in minor details
Voters are prohibited from reading political newspapers
questions.explanation: In recent years there has been a decline in the ideological differences among parties in most parts of the world. For example, the difference between the Labour Party and the Conservative Party in Britain is very little. In India too, the differences among all the major parties on the economic policies have reduced.
